one_liner: Ecommerce platform offering REST and GraphQL APIs for stores and apps.

evidence.claim: Authentication uses OAuth-based API accounts (store-level, app-level, account-level) with static access tokens for REST requests.
evidence.quote: BigCommerce offers three types of OAuth-based API accounts to developers who wish to use BigCommerce’s REST APIs: store-level credentials, app-level credentials, and account-level credentials.

evidence.claim: Credentials are created self-serve from the store control panel; developer docs also include a Sandboxes section for dev stores.
evidence.quote: Navigate to Settings > API Accounts in your store control panel. Create credentials with the scopes you need.

evidence.claim: Store-level credentials are generated by merchants in the control panel without sales or approval gates.
evidence.quote: Merchants generate single-store API credentials when they create API accounts in their store control panel, in the **[Settings > Store-level API accounts]

evidence.claim: API surface spans both REST and GraphQL with extensive endpoints (carts, checkouts, storefront, admin, B2B), indicating broad coverage.
evidence.quote: API Reference Complete REST and GraphQL API docs.

evidence.claim: BigCommerce officially documents an MCP server in its own API reference and AI agent setup for Cursor/Claude/Codex.
evidence.quote: AI Agent Setup Connect Cursor, Claude, or Codex to the BigCommerce developer docs via MCP.

notes: Vendor docs include a first-class MCP section (Overview, Tool Resynchronization, Storefront) in the API reference, plus /llms.txt and .md versions of pages for AI agents. Store-level access tokens do not expire and cannot be manually invalidated; some endpoints only accept one API account type. Sandbox free-ness is implied by the Sandboxes docs section but pricing is not stated in the supplied material.
